title.narrative: Inclusive Water Governance and Strengthening Climate Resilience in the Mekong Region

description.narrative: Building on previous Oxfam Inclusion Project, this investment has two complementary activities supporting civil society organizations (CSO) and community and women leaders to participate in water governance decision-making and strengthen community climate resilience in the Mekong sub-region. The investment supports civil society organizations partners, women leaders and communities in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam to engage with governments, inter-governmental bodies and the private sector in water resource governance, planning and development. It also supports targeted community and local authorities in the region to strengthen their disaster risk management and climate change adaptation through better access and use of hydro-meteorological data and awareness raising.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: In Cambodia, the Strengthening Climate Resilience in Lower Mekong (SCR) program strengthened community-based disaster management and improved early warning systems. It did this by enhancing the technical capacity of targeted communes to update their contingency plans in a more inclusive and responsive manner, and broadening access to early warning information through different channels, such as village speakers, mobile speakers, village information boards, and mobile phone devices.For example, the program supported the development and refinement of inclusive contingency plans in five targeted communes. It also supported 11 Village Disaster Management Groups to assess their climate risks, vulner abilities, capacities in distinct communities, and disastermanagement strategies. It did this by working with the local authorities and communities to examine their climate and disaster risks, strengthen early warning systems, organise awareness campaigns, and conduct simulation exercises.The program strengthened coordination and cooperation at the community level. When participating communities faced the risk of flooding in late 2024, local authorities and disaster groups put the plans into action. They translated alerts and disseminated them through fixed and mobile loudspeakers and social media, ensuring timely and accessible warnings for the community, and helping vulnerable groups get to safety.

The Inclusive Water Governance and Strengthening Climate Resilience in the Mekong Region Investment comprises two activities: Inclusion Project Phase 2 (IP2) and Strengthening Climate Resilience (SCR). ‍ The investment supported the Laos Disabled People Association (LDPA) and Cambodia’s Women with Disabilities Leadership and Advocacy Network (WWD-LAN) to strengthen capacities in creating an enabling environment for differing needs of people with disabilities. This involved learning and knowledge exchange to strengthen disability inclusion outcomes (eg. challenging and changing social norms, attitudes and behaviours).‍ LDPA developed assessment tools and monitored IP2 partners’ activities, emphasising the inclusion of People with Disabilities (PWD) in all aspects of planning, implementation and monitoring of project activities. LDPA conducted a training on disability inclusion in water governance which deepened participants' understanding on the needs and priorities of PWD and a joint commitment to promote active engagement in water governance.
